title: Google Brings Gemini 4 Argon to Android Development Tools
key_facts: Google's Android Developers Blog, dated 13 Oct 2026, says Gemini 4 Argon is available to Android developers.
Google describes Argon as strong at long-horizon autonomous execution and multi-step software tasks, and as generating production-ready Jetpack Compose code.
Antigravity, Google's agent workspace, runs across the desktop app, IDE extensions and the command line.
The official Android CLI plugin connects the agent to local Android tools.
Setup: run 'agy plugin install android-cli-plugin' in Antigravity or 'android init' for any terminal agent.
Argon is rolling out globally to developers in supported regions.
quote_evidence: Argon has significant improvements in long-horizon autonomous execution and the ability to plan and run multi-step, complex software tasks over time.
Argon demonstrates exceptional design craft, generating production-ready Jetpack Compose code out of the box.
Starting today, Argon is rolling out globally to developers in supported regions.
why_it_matters_hint: Android developers can use Google's newest model with agent tools that call Android's own command line.
notes: Technobezz page (403) not opened; read Google's original Android Developers Blog post instead. Google claims are unverified by outsiders. Event dated 13 Oct 2026.
